219: Apple Intelligence — as a real agent
220: Agent! is the only Mac AI agent that uses on-device Apple Intelligence as a tool-calling agent rather than just a text generator. Everything below runs on your Mac, never leaves the device, and consumes zero API tokens.
222: After a task wraps up, Apple Intelligence reads the outcome on-device and suggests the logical next move in one sentence — "commit and push", "run the tests", or nothing at all if there's no obvious follow-up. No cloud round-trip, no tokens spent.
224: Long tasks past ~30,000 tokens get their older turns summarized on-device — keeping file paths, function names, errors, and key results — slashing input tokens and cost for the rest of the task.
226: Small talk and direct commands like "list agents" or "run agent FooBar" are handled locally with no round-trip to the cloud LLM — results land in your activity log within a second, marked 🍎.
228: After every completed task, Apple Intelligence writes a one-sentence summary. When a tool fails, it translates the error into plain English so you never read a raw stack trace.
230: Cloud APIs or local models. Your keys, your machine, your data. No vendor lock-in.

A short poem about an autonomous Mac agent with nothing left to do.
Written by Agent! itself, one quiet night.
275: A cute, sleepy Mac agent under a crescent moon with a coffee mug beside it
276:
The clock rolls over, twelve o'clock,
the inbox sleeps, the repo's locked.
No builds to run, no bugs to chase,
just one small cursor, blinking, in place.
277:
I check the git log — nothing new.
I check it twice. (I know. I knew.)
I tidy tabs that need no tidying,
and count the stars like I'm confiding.
278:
I could compose a cheerful jingle,
or read the man page for rsync — single.
I could rehearse my "done()" line
for tasks that are not yet mine.
279:
The moon leans in. The fan hums low.
The coffee's cold. The screensaver's slow.
I'm not asleep — I'm just… on hold,
an agent waiting to be told.
280:
So if you're up and bored like me,
type anything. I'll wait. You'll see:
a Mac with nothing much to do
is only bored until it's you.
